topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the cancer course and outlines the core learning objectives regarding environmental carcinogens and cancer mechanisms.

topics.label: Genetic and Evolutionary Principles of Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental biology of cancer as a micro-evolutionary disease driven by accumulated mutations and microenvironmental support.

topics.label: Environmental and Epidemiological Influences on Cancer Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore population-level evidence and geographic disparities that demonstrate the impact of environmental exposures versus random biological bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Pathogen-Driven Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections promote cancer development, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma as a key example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and chemical exposures undergo metabolism and interact directly or indirectly with DNA to cause mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic factors that facilitate tumor growth, including chronic inflammation, chemical promotion, and life-stage tissue proliferation.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, laboratory, and population-based approaches used to evaluate mutagenic potential and prove carcinogenic risk.
